title: Context Helix: Low-overhead tracing hook and async-safe carrier library for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a compact, language-idiomatic tracing hook + carrier library (Context Helix) for our SDKs that provides deterministic context propagation across async boundaries with <0.25ms median added tail latency for common SDK hot paths. This ticket covers design, implementation in Node/Python/Go SDKs, cross-language test harness, backwards-compatible HTTP/gRPC header compatibility, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation API is exposed in Node/Python/Go SDKs with the same high-level surface (start/attach/flush).
End-to-end propagation verified across asynchronous boundaries (promises, goroutines, thread pools) in unit+integration tests.
Median added CPU/time per request is <0.25ms for 95% of observed traces on our internal perf harness (p99 <1.5ms).
Round-trip and forked-worker scenarios preserve trace IDs and span parent relationships without memory leaks.
Canary rollout plan executed with no customer-facing error rate increase >0.05% and latency increase <2.5% in canary cohort.
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and linked from SDK repos.
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer an in-process, allocation-minimizing carrier (compact binary token) for internal high-throughput paths and an HTTP header fallback for cross-process compatibility. Avoid global mutable state where possible; use explicit context objects per request for safety. We'll implement an optional no-op build flag for ultra-low overhead environments.
